questions.learningObjective: apply the doctrine of federalism to a concrete legal fact pattern
questions.stem: Consider this: A state legislature passing a law asks whether federal law preempts the state rule. Congress spoke expressly on the subject. Which statement best states the governing legal rule on these facts?

options.text: Preemption allows a state court to ignore a federal statute on these facts.
options.misconception: confuses preemption with supremacy clause rhetoric

options.text: Federal law displaces state law when Congress expressly says so or when federal regulation is so comprehensive that it leaves no room for state rules on these facts.
Any federal activity on a subject automatically nullifies all state law on that subject on these facts.
State law is never displaced unless Congress uses the word preempt on these facts.

questions.explanation: Preemption flows from the supremacy of valid federal law. It can be explicit or inferred from a scheme that occupies a field, but courts look for evidence that Congress meant to displace state authority. Here the decisive point is express and field preemption, so the result follows from that doctrine rather than from the surface appeal of a competing statement. Each distractor rests on a different mistake about how the doctrine operates.
questions.hint: Ask whether Congress meant to exclude state regulation, and how clearly. Keep the inquiry on express and field preemption.

questions.stem: Suppose this: A federal agency regulating an industry claims the state law burdens interstate trade. The state law is health and safety legislation. Which choice identifies the principle that controls the outcome here?

options.text: Congress may never regulate local activity even when aggregated it affects commerce as this record presents them.
options.misconception: assumes only interstate businesses are reachable

options.text: The commerce clause gives Congress the same general authority states have over health and safety as this record presents them.

Congress may regulate economic activity that substantially affects interstate commerce, but the connection to commerce must not be so attenuated that it becomes a general police power as this record presents them.
Congress may regulate any conduct anywhere because all activity affects commerce somehow as this record presents them.

questions.explanation: The commerce power is broad but not boundless. The regulated activity must have a real connection to interstate markets, and the chain of effects cannot be extended until every subject of life falls within federal authority. Here the decisive point is the commerce power and its limits, so the result follows from that doctrine rather than from the surface appeal of a competing statement. Each distractor rests on a different mistake about how the doctrine operates.
questions.hint: Ask whether the regulated activity itself is economic and substantially affects commerce. Keep the inquiry on the commerce power and its limits.

questions.subject: INTRO_LAW
questions.learningObjective: apply the doctrine of federalism to a concrete legal fact pattern
questions.stem: Now consider: A federal agency regulating an industry claims the state law burdens interstate trade. The state law is health and safety legislation. Which of the following is the correct legal conclusion under the described circumstances?

options.text: States may act only when federal law expressly authorizes them to do so under the circumstances described.
options.misconception: assumes states have no reserved authority

options.text: A state may restrict any activity however it wishes because health and safety are local under the circumstances described.
A state police power allows a state to nullify a conflicting federal statute under the circumstances described.
States retain authority to protect health, safety and welfare, subject to constitutional limits and valid federal laws that conflict with their rules under the circumstances described.

questions.explanation: Federalism leaves a domain of local regulation with the states. That authority is real but bounded: it cannot override constitutional rights or stand in the way of valid federal law. Here the decisive point is state police powers, so the result follows from that doctrine rather than from the surface appeal of a competing statement. Each distractor rests on a different mistake about how the doctrine operates.
questions.hint: Ask which sovereign has the stronger claim and why. Keep the inquiry on state police powers.

questions.learningObjective: apply the doctrine of federalism to a concrete legal fact pattern
questions.stem: Here instead: A federal agency regulating an industry claims the state law burdens interstate trade. The state law is health and safety legislation. Which answer choice correctly resolves the legal issue presented?

options.text: The federal government may generally encourage state cooperation but may not compel state officials to administer a federal regulatory program given the events just recounted.
Congress may order state agencies to enforce any federal scheme it creates given the events just recounted.
options.misconception: assumes federal government can direct state officers

options.text: A state that refuses to help administer a federal program is violating the constitution given the events just recounted.
Commandeering allows the federal government to displace state laws rather than conscript state officials given the events just recounted.

questions.explanation: Accountability matters in federalism. If state officials are forced to carry out federal policy, voters cannot tell which government is responsible, so the constitution treats compulsion of state administration differently from regulation of private parties. Here the decisive point is the anti-commandeering principle, so the result follows from that doctrine rather than from the surface appeal of a competing statement. Each distractor rests on a different mistake about how the doctrine operates.
questions.hint: Ask whether federal law regulates private conduct or commands state officers. Keep the inquiry on the anti-commandeering principle.

questions.learningObjective: apply the doctrine of federalism to a concrete legal fact pattern
questions.stem: The record: A federal agency regulating an industry claims the state law burdens interstate trade. The state law is health and safety legislation. Which account of the governing rule is faithful to the doctrine?

options.text: Preemption allows a state court to ignore a federal statute on these facts.
options.misconception: confuses preemption with supremacy clause rhetoric

options.text: Federal law displaces state law when Congress expressly says so or when federal regulation is so comprehensive that it leaves no room for state rules on these facts.
Any federal activity on a subject automatically nullifies all state law on that subject on these facts.
State law is never displaced unless Congress uses the word preempt on these facts.

questions.explanation: Preemption flows from the supremacy of valid federal law. It can be explicit or inferred from a scheme that occupies a field, but courts look for evidence that Congress meant to displace state authority. Here the decisive point is express and field preemption, so the result follows from that doctrine rather than from the surface appeal of a competing statement. Each distractor rests on a different mistake about how the doctrine operates.
questions.hint: Ask whether Congress meant to exclude state regulation, and how clearly. Keep the inquiry on express and field preemption.
